source.title: Galvanostatic Plating with a Single Additive Electrolyte for Bottom-Up Filling of Copper in Mesoscale TSVs

conditions.bath: 1.25 mol/L CuSO4 + 0.25 mol/L MSA + 1 mmol/L KCl + 50 umol/L Tetronic 701
conditions.hydrodynamics: die rotated 400 rpm on RDE rod (helicopter-blade mount); pre-wet: -18 C IPA under rough vacuum, direct transfer, 2 min at 400 rpm at -0.40 V to mix
conditions.vias: 100 um dia x 600 um deep (AR5), ALD Pt 60 nm seed + 300 nm Al2O3 liner, SOI substrate

data.result: all void-free fill; chronoamperometry measured (their Fig 4, curves not tabulated); effective j based on via bottom area only
void-free fill on all sizes; voltage within breakdown window

data.with_suppressor: 0.5-10 mA/cm2 for 2 h; nucleation needs slightly more negative E; 0.5 mA/cm2 shows destabilization/re-stabilization fluctuations; E varies only ~50 mV across j range; at 0.5 mA/cm2 minimum E ~ -0.6 V (SSE) near breakdown
data.without_suppressor: E varies >100 mV across same j range

data.result: characteristic S-NDR shape confirms bottom-up capability

notes: KEY calibration dataset for galvanostatic fill: 160 mA/cm2 (via-bottom basis, 400 rpm, ~295 K) is the void-free optimum for 100x600 um vias in 3 h. Voltages ~ breakdown potential (~-0.6 V SSE). Current density basis is via bottom area - important when mapping to platesim. Chronoamperometry curves in their Fig 4 could be digitised later (est. error +-2 mA/cm2, +-0.5 V).
